harbor_p21_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_001.text: Fen's trial assessment began in the twenty-third week with a page she had copied badly on her first day. The aunt placed it beside a recent checked column and asked her what had changed. Fen pointed to the figures, the spacing and the correction marks. The aunt asked about the habit beneath them. Fen thought before answering: she now asked when unsure, instead of making a quick neat guess. The answer mattered more than the clean page. The shop could teach speed. A hidden mistake could travel farther than a slow young clerk before anybody knew which hand to stop.

harbor_p21_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_002.text: The aunt offered a six-month paid apprenticeship under ordinary local terms. It included supervised account duties, stated hours and wages, and review dates rather than an immediate promise of permanent work. Fen would remain free to decline after reading it. She took the page home without signing because she wanted the choice to last long enough to feel like hers. Luo read it after supper and asked the actual lodging and return arrangements. The shop did not require her to move into the aunt's household. She could keep their current room while the lease and their private money allowed it.

harbor_p21_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_003.text: Fen wanted a small private shelf for her own learning pages. Luo said their room had a shelf. She said his fishing things occupied it. The objects were few and ordinary, and moving them still felt like losing an old claim on the room. He caught himself before saying a daughter should not need more space than a father. They rearranged the shelf together, keeping his personal comb and her practice book visible. A household could change by the width of a notebook. The apprenticeship page stayed unsigned on the table while the ordinary room slowly made space around it.

harbor_p21_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_004.text: Aning received a different assessment. She had advanced in dispatch comparison but still rushed explanations when other people failed to see what looked obvious to her. The aunt offered a continued account role with pay, not the same apprenticeship as Fen. Aning wanted titles because friendship made different labels feel like a ranking. The aunt asked whether the proposed duties matched her skills and wishes. They did. It took Aning longer to answer that than to check the numbers. Her friend's opportunity did not make her own work smaller unless she insisted on reading the two pages as a contest.

harbor_p21_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_005.text: The girls met at the safe shore wall after work. Fen wanted to celebrate and feared Aning would resent it. Aning wanted to complain and feared Fen would call her ungrateful. They said both things badly, then tried again. Fen described the shelf. Aning described the explanation duty. Eventually they laughed about the aunt asking habits when everyone wanted to discuss titles. Their friendship had survived searches, family worry and ordinary envy. It might survive different work too, provided neither claimed affection meant the other should always know how to speak without causing discomfort.

harbor_p21_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_006.text: He Ming returned through the ordinary licensed route with her visit completed and Jun's latest household message expected at its agreed interval. Zhou met her at the quay only after her own work finished. Their first words concerned the ferry's delay and the ugly gull's safe wrapping. Then He Ming asked what had changed. Zhou gave the actual corrected lease page and the buyer's final offer, including Ke's paid trial. The partnership had waited for the required consent and continued its ordinary tasks. He Ming felt relieved and slightly unnecessary, a combination her mother would have recognized instantly.

harbor_p21_007.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p21_007.text: I am glad you did not turn waiting for my reply into waiting for me to make every ordinary decision. The corrected page matches what we agreed. Let us read the final start and payment dates together before money moves. I have brought stories from my mother, and I would like to tell them over lunch after the work. She says your argument about prices sounds like a woman who knows what soup costs. I think this is praise. She also says I should stop translating all family wisdom into partnership instructions. Please remind me of that before I begin.

harbor_p21_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_008.text: The new agreement guaranteed four modest batches across eight weeks, with actual cancellation terms and separate checks for each. Each batch's ninety-six price covered materials twenty-four, rented space sixteen and wages forty-eight, leaving an eight margin only after completion and all costs. The three partners would receive twelve each; Ke's four paid half-days at three made twelve. The landlord's eight-week space term cost sixty-four across the four stated batch intervals, begun under the conditional sequence already agreed. They signed after the ordinary room check and buyer acceptance. No future margin was called cash they already held.

harbor_p21_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_009.text: The first forty-eight advance arrived through the buyer's own account. Twenty-four bought materials, sixteen paid the first space interval, and eight paid two initial wage copper to each of four workers. The later forty-eight balance would pay their remaining forty wages and leave the earned eight margin if the batch was accepted. Ke's paid trial began under that actual source, with the ordinary tools checked out for the job. He Ming hung the ugly gull in the new room after the landlord permitted its removable nail. The board looked worse against clean plaster. Everybody agreed this proved continuity of management.

harbor_p21_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_010.text: An wanted to keep the gull's old smoke stain visible. Han, visiting privately after work, said its current artistic condition could not be improved without a new kind of miracle. Yue arrived with her familiar cup and was told to sit outside the production lane as usual. The larger room had made this easier, which she appreciated. Ke examined the ordinary check table and set the job's supplied needle beside it. Her personally bought needle remained in her own sewing bag. A new workplace could provide tools without taking possession of the little object she had bought to begin again.

harbor_p21_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_011.text: The first trial task required Ke to check a row of ties before the partners closed the outer parcels. She spotted an inconsistent mark and asked whether it reflected two delivery groups. It did, but the separation instruction was poorly placed on the task sheet. He Ming thanked her and moved the explanation before the actual work sequence continued. Zhou said the table had acquired another pair of inconvenient eyes. Ke asked whether inconvenience affected the rate. An said only if she discovered he had tied the wrong group. They laughed and made the correction where everyone could see it.

harbor_p21_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_012.text: Wu came for lunch after the canteen stock task ended. She admired the room and declined to feel responsible for its fifth chair. Her work remained the canteen with occasional packing only when offered hours fit. The partners bought the ordered food at its price. She told He Ming the duck had protested her absence by overturning a cup nobody admitted placing within reach. He Ming described her mother's soup judgment. They laughed together, then spoke seriously about the visit. Wu said returning to chosen work sounded easier after sitting beside a parent who knew how to let her leave.

harbor_p21_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_013.text: He Ming said leaving had been hard and different from abandoning. Jun had his own life, their mother her own preferences, and the neighbors bounded help they actually accepted. She had not acquired authority over any of them by traveling inland. Wu asked whether she had wanted to. He Ming admitted yes. The conversation stayed private over lunch, while the partners prepared the next actual work interval. Yue heard only the story He Ming later chose to share. He Ming carried the rest of the conversation home privately, where the plant waited beside Jun's letters.

harbor_p21_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_014.text: At the account shop, Fen signed the apprenticeship after reading the final terms and confirming the pay and review dates. Luo attended only the explanation she invited him to hear. The aunt asked Fen for the answer and Fen gave it. Her father looked proud, then tired. Outside he said he wished he had been present for more of the learning that brought her here. She answered that she wished it too. The regret did not make the signature less hers. They walked home with the copy in her hands and no claim that reunion had returned every lost month.

harbor_p21_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_015.text: That evening Luo showed her a letter from Reed Steps. The timber camp had a record-sorting opening after another clerk's departure, with no heavy saw or loading duty in its proposed terms. The employer knew his hand restrictions from the information he consented to share. He had not accepted. He wanted to consider it after the harbor season and care review. Fen read the page twice. Reed Steps had been the place where his silence nearly swallowed their family. A named job and contact made it different, but her body had not learned the difference as quickly as her eyes.

harbor_p21_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_016.text: Luo said he would not leave before discussing the plan, and any travel would need his care clearance, money and local work agreement. Fen asked why he wanted to return at all. He said he had friends there and unfinished ordinary wishes, not a debt to the machine that injured him. He also wanted to work where people knew a skill beyond being somebody's recovered father. The sentence hurt her until she recognized a wish similar to her own apprenticeship. She did not approve the plan. She agreed they could keep talking while neither had signed away the next season.

harbor_p21_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_017.text: Yue met Fen the following morning practicing a column in her personal book. The girl asked whether love always made people want different roads. Yue said she did not know always, and described her own decision to leave after the term. Fen looked annoyed that adults kept refusing useful universal answers. Then she laughed. Yue asked about the apprenticeship's first task rather than her father's letter. Fen wanted to explain it. The conversation gave her a place to be ambitious without spending the whole morning defending how ambition could coexist with wanting her father nearby.

harbor_p21_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_018.text: Aning's father heard about her account role and said his shop could use her skill now that it had grown. She reminded him the aunt's bounded contract was the work she had chosen. He said family should have first claim on learning it helped make possible. The argument returned with words and a more adult daughter. Aning did not deny his support. She asked whether support had been a loan with terms nobody told her. He fell silent. The private business history would not be settled by one sentence, but the question made the next supper honest enough to begin.

harbor_p21_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_019.text: The aunt arranged a permitted discussion after Aning requested help explaining the actual work commitment to her father. She did not become his daughter's permanent guardian or negotiator. The father attended voluntarily, heard the terms and asked about a future interval when Aning might quote a separate paid task for his shop. Aning said she could consider it if her own schedule allowed. Family work would then be real work, with duties and pay, not a test of whether she loved him enough to abandon another promise. He disliked the condition and eventually asked what rate the task might require.

harbor_p21_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_020.text: Fen watched Aning return from the discussion with a strange expression. The girl said her father had asked about a price instead of demanding an evening. Fen congratulated her. Aning said it felt terrible to be congratulated for something that ought to have been simple. They laughed without much pleasure, then took out their private practice pages. The numbers required less emotional interpretation than households, though neither would say so inside a customer's hearing. By the time the kettle was ready, they had solved one sum and failed another. A future could proceed through that uneven ordinary rhythm.

harbor_p21_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_021.text: At the property office, the warehouse's final notice interval approached with twenty loss copper still held. One additional eligible claimant supplied a surviving receipt for small damaged storage goods assessed at four. Hao received the supporting comparison and did not contest the actual amount. The custodian paid four, bringing loss payments to sixty-four and balance to sixteen. The remaining sixteen would return only after the stated interval and unresolved-question notice closed properly. The private building account still held thirty-two after its one hundred four spending. Neither remainder became a general fund for whatever the harbor next found sad.

harbor_p21_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_022.text: The warehouse plan's smaller footprint included a reporting position near the usable doorway. A person unable to write could ask the keeper to record a concern and receive an identified next step. The staff duty and check time came from Hao's operating arrangement, not the proposed public sixty-four pilot still unapproved. Bao's earlier oral complaint had helped expose the old gap. She was not required to staff its remedy. Hao asked whether she wanted to inspect the explanation from the public side when care allowed. Bao chose a later date, retaining the right not to turn recovery into free consultation.

harbor_p21_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_023.text: Bao's small net work continued only within the care plan and paid offers. Dai kept the next customer's terms clear before asking her. The work did not mean her cough had vanished or her warehouse lost-work claim was settled. She sat with her cousin reading the latest review notice and then put it aside to mend a household sleeve. Her needle moved through familiar cloth. The cousin asked whether she was tired and accepted the yes. A person could earn two copper on one day and need company doing nothing on the next without making the first day a lie.

harbor_p21_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_024.text: Yan received the platform hearing source schedule and gave his ordinary crew duties to the assigned cover for that interval. Deren arranged his independent explanation appointment. They did not travel together, because their actual questions involved different interests even while their friendship continued. Bo wanted to accompany both and discovered that was physically impossible. Deren told him to remain where the roster paid him and send a decent joke afterward. The boy said decent jokes were beyond the present rate. Yan laughed, then went to check the ordinary kit, whose worn pencil needed replacing from the crew's proper supply.

harbor_p21_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_025.text: Sui practiced her account of the platform duty dates in a room and stopped when it began sounding like a speech. The officer needed sources, not a captain making herself admirable through readiness to suffer. She separated memory from record again and placed both in their proper order. At supper she told Han she feared she would either defend too much or apologize beyond what she knew. The clerk said questions would help keep the scope clear if she answered them. Sui laughed that this advice sounded infuriatingly sensible from somebody she once taught to keep a public heading modest.

harbor_p21_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_026.text: Han said she still needed the teaching. Her wage desk had received a new inquiry with no connection to the original thirteen cases, and she had almost assumed a familiar family name gave her the missing consent. The ordinary check caught the gap before information moved. She reported the near error through the actual office routine and kept the private household out of supper conversation. Sui appreciated the admission and asked no details she did not need. Yue listened nearby as a friend. Competence could include saying where a familiar habit nearly outran the question in front of it.

harbor_p21_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_027.text: Qin returned from his approved inland visit with the song's disputed last line still unresolved. His sister had supplied a version he considered historically implausible and emotionally superior. Han said this was the first useful standard he had brought to a wage office. He laughed and accepted the handover from the replacement custodian. The misplaced source had been corrected and logged, not hidden. Qin thanked him for the account. Then he went home to the neighbor-watered beans and discovered one leaf chewed. He suspected a slug rather than a malicious institutional failure, which pleased everyone when he told the story.

harbor_p21_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_028.text: Duan offered Han another future lettering task, but its proposed hours conflicted with the clerk's ordinary receiving shift. Han declined that timing and asked whether a later small task might fit. The painter agreed to ask when actual work arose. The refusal felt less frightening than Yue's declined guard lead had sounded. Han now understood the narrow question: she could want a trade without taking every opportunity before it vanished. She had a room she chose to keep and a desk she still wanted. A private pleasure did not need to swallow both in order to count as growth.

harbor_p21_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_029.text: At the new partnership room, the first batch continued through its two-week schedule. Ke had completed two of her four paid half-days, with the initial two wage copper already received and the remaining total due through the balance process. The current material, rent and wage advance remained forty-eight; the future balance was not spent in anticipation. Zhou checked the private notebook and showed He Ming the progress. An said the clean plaster made the gull look professionally disreputable. They laughed and resumed work, their venture neither a miracle nor the small abandoned table He Ming once feared it might become.

harbor_p21_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_030.text: Fen ended the apprenticeship's first day with a task page checked and a question she would ask tomorrow. Luo had supper ready at their agreed room. She wanted to tell him every figure and found herself talking instead about the window, Aning's annoyance and the aunt's habit of tapping the table twice before speaking. He listened. His possible Reed Steps work remained only a proposal. Her actual apprenticeship had begun. The two facts could sit together without demanding that one road erase the other. They ate ordinary bread while the coast's light shortened beyond the closed shutter.

harbor_p21_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_031.text: The repair shed boy announced his birthday three times before anyone asked the date. His mother said it was tomorrow and he had already consumed most of the available anticipation. He wanted the fish kite flown from the inland common, where his parent had arranged the afternoon gathering away from quay work. Fen promised to come after her apprenticeship shift. Aning checked her actual closing time before agreeing. Bo said adults required a receipt for birthdays now. The boy demanded one immediately, with the age written larger than the name. His mother laughed and sent him to fetch clean cups.

harbor_p21_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_032.text: Yue helped carry the household's light basket on the permitted common path after work. It contained private food, the folded kite and enough cheap cups to make the handle creak. The boy tried to follow with a stool too large for his arms. His mother took it from him and gave him the spool. He protested that the important person had received the smallest load. Han said importance was best measured by the trouble someone made if his load was lost. The boy examined the spool with new gravity and walked ahead, nearly solemn for six entire steps.

harbor_p21_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_033.text: At the common a goat had escaped the tether and was considering the birthday table as an invitation. Its owner pursued it with the defeated voice of a man whose property had more appetite than discipline. Bo offered to help and was told to stand clear of the rope loop while the owner retrieved it from the safe side. The goat left with a leaf in its mouth. The boy said this was worse than piracy because the leaf had belonged to nobody. Aning asked whether that made it better. He said no, it made the thief harder to charge.

harbor_p21_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_034.text: The kite rose on the second attempt. Its tail whispered over the dry grass, then snapped straight above the common. Fen held the spool while the boy ran within the marked open space his parent allowed. He shouted each private passenger name as if the paper could hear better than the people below. Han stood beside Yue with her scarf tucked close against the wind. The painted fish tipped toward the sea without approaching the working quay. For a moment its ridiculous fins looked almost competent. The boy cried that it had finally learned where its own face belonged.

harbor_p21_035.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p21_035.text: That makes one of us. I have been drawing a boat all month and still put its curve in places the actual boat would object to. Yue, do not look so pleased by this confession. You folded one parcel badly and behaved as if you had discovered leisure. Fen, bring it a little lower before the line catches that branch. There, that's better. I am going to eat the bun I paid for before the goat returns with a superior claim. If anybody writes a register of this afternoon, put me down as occupied with filling.

harbor_p21_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_036.text: The boy's mother had made a cake whose surface leaned toward one edge. She said the pan had been uneven; Bo said the cake might simply prefer the sea. The boy demanded a corner with more paste. His mother cut it and gave the next piece to herself. Nobody argued about fairness after seeing her expression. Fen ate beside Aning and asked how long they would remain friends when their work became different. Aning stared at her with crumbs on her lip. She said they could at least wait until the birthday was over before opening such a large account.

harbor_p21_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_037.text: Fen laughed and stole one of Aning's crumbs with the shameless familiarity she had feared losing. The girl swatted her hand. Their work pages would have different headings tomorrow; today their argument concerned who had first insulted the cake. Yue sat on the low wall watching Luo teach the boy a sound ordinary knot without straining his injured hand. He used the spool's light cord and stopped when the careful motion tired him. The boy thanked him by saying his knot looked old. Luo answered that old knots were often the ones still holding when young knots became interesting stories.

harbor_p21_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_038.text: Luo's remark sounded grand enough that Fen groaned. He grinned and said fathers acquired the right to irritate daughters by surviving their own foolishness. She said he had overqualified. The humor trembled at its edge and held. They had not forgotten the silence from Reed Steps. They were tired of asking every light word to prove it had been forgiven. Luo let the boy unwind the knot under his mother's eye and sat beside his daughter. He asked whether her apprenticeship stool was comfortable. She said the stool had excellent opinions about posture and expressed them through splinters.

harbor_p21_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_039.text: Peng offered to examine the shop's stool only if its owner requested a repair task. Fen said she could pass that offer on; she had no authority to hire him for the aunt. He accepted the answer and asked whether the cake came with a report. The boy handed him a piece too thin to support inspection. Peng ate it and pronounced the contents sound. Wen, arriving after her workshop closed, brought an orange and complained that every carpenter in the harbor believed he could judge pastry. Peng said pastry rarely required a plane, which made it merciful work.

harbor_p21_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_040.text: He Ming arrived with Zhou, both carrying the food they had agreed to contribute privately. An had an outside shift and sent a bun with no apology for choosing wages over the gathering. Wu came later with the children and no duck; the bird's basket remained attended at their room by the neighbor under the short visit. Everyone seemed disappointed by its absence. Wu said she had not brought the canteen's stock either and wished people would stop treating her most troublesome possession as the guest of honor. The birthday boy accepted this only after receiving another piece of cake.

harbor_p21_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_041.text: Under the wind, He Ming told Han she wanted a plain public sign for North Quay Packing. Han asked whether this was a private favor or a commission. He Ming said a commission, with actual work and payment outside the clerk shift. Duan would check the lettering as agreed, and the owner of the practice materials would supply the board under the quote. Four copper was accepted for the bounded task, paid from the partners' own agreed personal shares before any unearned batch margin. Han looked pleased enough that Zhou asked whether the ugly gull would charge a consultation fee.

harbor_p21_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_042.text: Han said the gull had retained all its royalties by being too bad to reproduce. The new sign would use letters and no bird pretending to authorize anything. He Ming wanted the room number easy to read. Zhou wanted the receiving hours. An had sent one instruction: make the letters less crooked than the supervisor's eyes. They laughed and wrote the specification on Han's scrap with the parties' consent. Yue watched the three women make a job from affection without asking affection to do the job for free. Then she stopped watching because the birthday boy needed a kite launch.

harbor_p21_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_043.text: The wind dropped halfway through the next launch, leaving the fish sliding toward the grass. The boy wanted Bo to run faster. Bo said paper possessed no obligation to birthdays. They tried again after an ordinary pause and got a shorter flight. The boy accepted it with the misery of somebody discovering weather had not read his invitation. His mother wrapped the kite before dusk and promised nothing about tomorrow's wind. He carried it home himself, proud enough to complain. Yue followed with the now lighter basket, whose ordinary handle seemed grateful to contain empty cups rather than a future.

harbor_p21_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_044.text: At the account shop the next morning, Fen delivered Peng's offer about the stool. The aunt authorized a maintenance visit and price before work. Peng found one loose fastening and a rough edge; the repair came from the shop's account. Fen was not charged for noticing it. She sat down afterward and nearly laughed at how little pain good furniture caused. Aning asked whether the apprenticeship had improved overnight. Fen said the arithmetic remained offensive, but its chair had become willing. Their task sheets waited. They started under the trained employee's check, not under the carpenter's opinion of their future.

harbor_p21_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_045.text: The aunt's next customer asked Fen a question beyond her assigned scope. Fen called the trained employee instead of guessing. The man sighed about apprentices wasting time. The employee answered the actual account question and explained Fen's role plainly. After he left, Fen wanted to defend herself to an empty doorway. Aning handed her the next practice page and said the sigh had not changed the figures. Fen completed the column slowly. She would hear that kind of impatience again, which was a duller prospect than becoming brilliantly competent overnight. At closing she still liked the work.

harbor_p21_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_046.text: Luo received the Reed Steps employer's proposed terms by the permitted contact route. The work remained light record sorting, with lodging and a bounded term stated. His care reviewer still needed to assess travel and sustained hand use at the later interval. He did not sign a departure before that answer. Fen read the lodging line and asked whether he would know the neighbor in the next room. He did. She wanted to ask ten more questions and chose the one that mattered: whether he actually wanted this or merely wanted a place where his old shame was less visible.

harbor_p21_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_047.text: Her father thought before answering. He wanted the work and feared her seeing him choose it. Both were true. He had been injured there, silent afterward and found again by a daughter who had grown without his permission. Returning might let him live differently; it could also be an attempt to tidy the memory. Fen said he should speak to the care reviewer and the employer before deciding which hope was carrying the cart. Luo laughed at the image and thanked her. She had begun giving adult advice, and neither wanted that to become her permanent unpaid task.

harbor_p21_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_048.text: At the partnership's first regular batch, Ke completed the third of her four paid half-days. Her motions suited the current care limits, and the partners kept the ordinary rest interval inside the schedule. The actual balance had not arrived yet because completion and acceptance lay in the next week. Two wage copper had been paid to each worker from the advance; the remaining ten each stayed due under the written terms. An complained that promised money always seemed more impatient than finished parcels. Ke said she preferred a visible due date to a buyer who called every delay a misunderstanding.

harbor_p21_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_049.text: Miao checked the receiver's appointment with the buyer and learned its usual representative would be away. He obtained the substitute's authority before the batch finished. Zhou appreciated this more than a polite assurance the buyer remained interested. The agent had acquired an irritating habit of pointing at dates, which now served their business rather than his old incentive. He told Yue over tea that being useful looked less impressive than he expected. She asked whether he wanted impressive or paid. He answered both, then laughed because the honest reply made him sound more ordinary than either of them once allowed.

harbor_p21_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_050.text: The cloth trader's daughter asked for a future quote from the partnership after their capacity allowed it. He Ming gave the current receiving hours and earliest available interval beyond the guaranteed work, with no implied priority because the trader had lost stock. The daughter accepted and said she preferred a clear refusal to hopeful scheduling. Her father still resented their earlier rejection. She did not ask the partners to fix that feeling before doing business. The new request might become a contract later. For now it was an ordinary conversation between people whose disaster had not made them identical allies.

harbor_p21_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_051.text: Hao's loss custodian closed the proper notice interval after the supported outstanding payment and stated review routes were resolved. Sixty-four had been paid from the eighty account. The sixteen remainder returned to Hao's trading account with the actual closure record, rather than becoming new building cash. The rebuilding account remained separate: sources one hundred thirty-six, spent one hundred four, balance thirty-two. Yue checked only the public closure explanation during her appointment. Private ownership had not changed because an award was public. The cloth trader's further profit question still had its documented route if he chose to use it.

harbor_p21_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_052.text: The returned sixteen disappointed the steward, who had already imagined a new coat for the keeper as a symbol of restored confidence. Hao told him symbols needed a private choice and actual price, not an unspent claimant balance renamed before its notice ended. She then asked the keeper whether he needed ordinary protective clothing under his employment terms. He did. The proper operating purchase was arranged from its own authorized private line, with no invented charge to loss custody. The steward complained that his idea had been good. Hao agreed the need was real and the proposed source wrong.

harbor_p21_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_053.text: Bao visited the warehouse reporting doorway on the later date she had chosen after care clearance. The owner had arranged an explanation task under actual private terms if her participation was used, rather than expect free testimony disguised as gratitude. Bao asked how a spoken latch concern reached the maintenance keeper. The employee showed the entry and receiving acknowledgment. She tested the explanation as an ordinary speaker who did not write easily. It worked this time. She did not certify the whole building safe. She left with her agreed task payment and the care rest interval still hers to keep.

harbor_p21_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_054.text: Dai waited for her beyond the site boundary by invitation, carrying no work demand. They went to a stall for tea bought with their own money. Bao said the doorway had felt strange even though she remained outside the damaged interior. Dai said returning to places after loss could make ordinary objects look newly impolite. Bao laughed at that and then grew quiet. They spoke about nets until the interval required heading back. Yue saw them on the road and waved without joining. Not every useful friendship needed the traveler at its center or a report at her desk afterward.

harbor_p21_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_055.text: Han's North Quay Packing sign was checked by Duan and accepted by the partners under the four-copper task. The public letters named the room, trade and actual receiving hours. There was no guild seal or quarantine claim. They paid the private agreed four and kept the sign as their business property. Han brought her earned fee home and showed Yue the stained finger that would not wash clean. The traveler called it evidence of artistic employment. Han said she was more interested in evidence of supper. They bought bread and ordinary soup, leaving the new room to its own evening.

harbor_p21_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_056.text: Before the twenty-fourth-week hearing, Yue's two scheduled half-days earned another four copper. Six paid the agreed bed and meals. Twenty-two half-days had now been paid in the new appointment. Spending reached one hundred twenty-eight, leaving seventy-two: wages twelve, bed eighteen, ferry eighteen, copies twelve, interpretation twelve. No new field cost came from that term this week. The emergency reserve remained one hundred seventy-two spent and sixty-eight unspent, with four unused stones. She copied the balances into her personal account and placed the official hearing route back with its keeper, where tomorrow's participants could actually receive it.

harbor_p21_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_057.text: At dusk Fen stood on the shore wall with Aning watching boats return along the open channel. One vessel's lantern looked like a moving doorway. Fen said she once believed finding her father would tell her where home was. Aning asked whether it had. The girl answered that it told her he was alive and now they had to choose the rest. The words sounded bleak until she smiled. Her apprenticeship would begin again tomorrow, and her father might take another road later with a real address. The sea kept moving while two friends planned where to buy cheap supper.

harbor_p21_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p21_058.text: Yue ended the twenty-third week at Han's table, where the sign fee lay in the clerk's purse and the personal notebook occupied its shelf. Neither woman spoke about leaving until the kettle was empty. Then Han asked which ordinary address Yue wanted used for their first permitted road reply. The traveler did not yet know. They agreed she would send the receiving place when it existed, and no one would invent it now. The unfinished detail felt less frightening after being said. Outside, a porter called the tide reading down the lane, and another voice repeated it through the cold.
